$comment_dontKnow: PERSONA v3.2 §2 Law 8, under a heading that reads 'absolute, no exceptions': "'Nahi pata'
is a complete answer. Accept it, move on, never re-ask, never teach, never sound let down."
Owner ruling 2026-07-31 separated the two cases that used to be conflated:
* an EXPLICIT don't-know is an ANSWER — the answer being 'unknown' — and closes ANY topic,
not just the three in negation.json's negationAnswersTopics;
* a reply the detector simply could not KEY is a different situation, and INTERVIEW-1's
bounded re-ask (with the topic's retry_question) still owns it.
DELIBERATELY NOT IN HERE. The cost is asymmetric — a missed close is recoverable (the worker
is asked once more), a wrongly-closed essential is not (the topic is never re-asked and the
value is lost) — so every ambiguous form is left out.
'yaad nahi' / 'yad nahi' ('don't remember'). EXCLUDED. It reads as a don't-know in
isolation, but the corpus contains certifications: 'certificate hai par naam yaad nahi'
— a worker who HAS a certificate and cannot recall its name — and that string keys
NOTHING today (measured: {}), so the `not in answered` guard would not have saved it.
Including it would have closed the certifications topic for a worker who explicitly
said they hold one. Not remembering the NAME of a thing you have is not the same as
not knowing.
bare 'nahi'. EXCLUDED, and the task explicitly allowed leaving it out. To an open question
('Kaunsi machine?') it is not a don't-know at all, and to a yes/no question it is a
DENIAL, which negation.json's negatableTopicCues already handles for the topics where a
denial is a complete answer. There is no reading of a bare 'nahi' that is safe across
all fourteen topics.
Verified against the 314-fixture answer corpus: 3 hits, all of them fixtures a human already

$comment_hardship: §5: 'Says work has been hard -> One line, <=8 words, no advice: "Samajh sakta hoon."
THE HARD PART IS THE FALSE POSITIVE, not the match. Consoling a worker who just told you
about a promotion is a worse failure than saying nothing, and the sheet's own logic applies
('faked fluency is worse than plainness'). So this is a list of PHRASES that can only be
about personal hardship, never single words:
'mushkil' alone is unusable — 'setting mushkil hoti hai par kar leta hu' is a worker
describing DIFFICULT WORK, which is closer to a capability claim than to hardship. Only
'ghar chalana mushkil' (and its variants) is anchored to the person.

The original used \d+ for the duration. Python's \d is Unicode-aware and JavaScript's is
ASCII-only, so it is spelled out as ASCII digits PLUS the Devanagari digit range
(U+0966-U+096F) — the only other digit set this corpus contains.

gratuitous tonal shift on an innocent worker; the whole benefit is small (one neutral
acknowledgement instead of the default one), so the bar for inclusion is that the token
cannot plausibly occur in shop-floor text.

$comment_firstPersonClaim: TD98 / TD101. Does the worker claim this of THEMSELVES, or are they describing a workplace,
a relative, or an ambition? `hasFirstPersonClaim` is true when `firstPersonClaim` matches
This is what stops 'humare yahan CNC hai' becoming trade: CNC operator, and 'bhai welder
hai' becoming a welder profile. The blockers cover three distinct false-positive families
and all three were real: THIRD PARTIES (bhai, baap, dost, pati, biwi), ASPIRATION (chahta,
banna — wanting to become something is not being it), and TRAINING (seekh, training — 'CNC
seekh raha hu' carries a first-person marker AND is not a capability claim).
Blocker-wins is deliberate and asymmetric: writing a machine the worker never claimed into
their profile sends them to the wrong job, while dropping one costs a follow-up question.
$comment_correctionMarkers: P1-1: an EXPLICIT self-correction. Only these let a value for a topic that is NOT the one
being asked overwrite an already-collected value (see interview_engine's _may_commit).
Plain lowercase SUBSTRINGS, not regexes — matched with a case-folded `in` check, so
'correct kar' also covers 'correct karo' / 'correct karna'. Substring semantics are load
-bearing here and must not be quietly upgraded to word-boundary matching.
